summary: State fire tower completed about 1927 near the Cheat River canyon, 65 ft; site now part of Snake Hill WMA; state list marks it gone. No removal date found in sources read.

access.note: Site is publicly owned as part of Snake Hill Wildlife Management Area (FFLOS)

facts.agency: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources

events.note: Completed by the State of West Virginia circa 1927; 65 feet of angle iron; ground secured on a 99-year lease by the state fish and game commission
May 1934 report: rangers at the tower said a man suspected of setting three fires had been trailed into Pennsylvania
Registered January 26, 2017 as US 1660, WV 51; nominated by Brian M. Powell

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Forest Lookouts say Monongalia County; the state list says Preston. Snake Hill WMA lies in both counties. The record keeps Monongalia, matching the register.
The register names the West Virginia Division of Natural Resources; the 1927 item names the state fish and game commission as the lessee of the ground. The story reports both as the sources do.

notes_for_editor: No removal year or cause in any source read, so the story says only that the state list marks it gone. No source describes what remains on the site. Brief's county (Monongalia) kept; firelookout.org state list says Preston. Mountain Travel Guide acreage (2,000) differs from Wikipedia (3,092); not used. AllTrails page returned 403 and was not read.
